size.evidence: network_game_add_player copies exactly 0x20 bytes into each of 16 slots at game+0x226; network_player_reset accesses through offset 0x1f

stride.evidence: network_game_add_player, network_game_remove_player, and network_game_invalidate_machine advance player slots by 0x20

fields.name: name
fields.evidence: network_game_client_add_player passes record+0x00 to ustrncpy with count 0xb, and network_game_client_add_player_to_game logs the record as a player identity

fields.name: field_18
fields.evidence: network_game_client_add_player stores a 16-bit profile value at +0x18; network_game_server_add_player_to_game tests the same offset against -1

fields.name: field_1a
fields.evidence: network_game_client_add_player stores 0xffff at +0x1a; no semantic meaning is proven

fields.name: machine_index
fields.evidence: network_player_is_valid range-checks signed byte +0x1c; logs and comparisons identify it as the machine index

fields.name: controller_index
fields.evidence: network_player_is_valid range-checks signed byte +0x1d; logs call it controller index and network_game_client_add_player writes the local player index

fields.name: team_index
fields.evidence: network_game_dump logs signed byte +0x1e as team_index; network_game_client_add_player initializes it from the profile record

fields.name: player_index
fields.evidence: network_game_add_player uses signed byte +0x1f to select the destination slot and network_game_spawn_player updates it from player_new

notes: Offsets 0x00-0x17 are a packed wide-character name plus terminator area; the record artifact claims only the observed 16-bit accesses and the 11-word copy range.
The source uses byte accesses for indices, and the original disassembly uses signed byte tests/MOVSX at these offsets.
